title: Capture updated state in closures and rerender without destroying sibling UI state
trigger: A vanilla-DOM popup/component uses helper functions that return a new immutable state object, and callbacks close over a mutable `state` variable; rerendering the active component must not destroy appended siblings (e.g., candidate list)
principle: When state helpers return a new state object (immutable update), the callback that calls them must assign the return value back to the closed-over variable (`state = update(state)`). The helper itself must pass the new state to any rerender it triggers. The rerender function should replace only the piece that changed (e.g., the winner candidate) and preserve sibling DOM nodes instead of clearing the whole container, so appended candidates and their local state survive.

cases.context: Popup dictionary: status cycle and definition toggle callbacks were calling helpers but discarding the returned state, and rerender cleared the entire candidate list

applyFor: Vanilla-DOM components with mutable state shared by closures
Lists where rerendering an item must keep other items mounted
Popup/modal content that appends additional results while keeping winner state
